html:
A Tamil empire of south India, ruled by the Chola dynasty from 848 to 1279. At its height it was a sea power whose fleets reached Sri Lanka, the Maldives and Southeast Asia.

The Cholas were an old name, one of the three Tamil royal houses of ancient times. Their revival began in 848, when Vijayalaya took Thanjavur. In 897 his son defeated the Pallavas.

The two great kings:

  • Rajaraja I (985 to 1014) conquered the Pandyas and Cheras, northern Sri Lanka and the Maldives. He built the Brihadisvara Temple at Thanjavur, finished in 1010, with a tower about 66 metres high.
  • Rajendra I (1014 to 1044) took all of Sri Lanka, ending the Anuradhapura kingdom, and marched north to the Ganges. He built a new capital, Gangaikonda Cholapuram, "the city of the Chola who took the Ganges". In 1025 his fleet raided Srivijaya, the trading empire that controlled the Strait of Malacca.

The Cholas sent embassies to Song China, and Tamil merchant guilds traded across the Bay of Bengal. At home, inscriptions record village assemblies that chose their members by lot and managed land, water tanks and temples. The age is famous for its bronze sculpture, above all the dancing Shiva, Nataraja.

In 1070 the Chola throne passed to a prince of the Eastern Chalukya line, Kulothunga I, and Sri Lanka broke free the same year. The empire held on for two more centuries but slowly lost ground to the Hoysalas and to the reviving Pandyas, who ended Chola rule in 1279.
sum: A Tamil empire of south India, ruled by the Chola dynasty from 848 to 1279. At its height it was a sea power whose fleets reached Sri Lanka, the Maldives and Southeast Asia.
